# Restyling an installed app with a skin

To rename, re-icon or re-theme an installed app ("make the Slack app look like
Discord") you write ordinary records. There is no rebuild, reinstall or Adopt, and
the open app repaints in place, keeping its current view and drafts. It needs a host that
supports `app.skin.v1` (the hosted workbench and Shell); an older host ignores skins. On
such a host a skin does three separate things, and only one depends on the app:

- **Name and icon** (`display_name`, `icon`) apply to any installed app.
- **CSS** (`css`) applies to any app, written against whatever selectors it has.
- **Tokens and labels** only take effect where the app declares them: its `--app-*`
  properties and `native-skin-labels` table (for Slack, version 0.5.0 or later). An app
  without those hooks ignores them without error.

So do not refuse a rename, re-icon or CSS-only restyle because the app is not skin-ready.

## What a skin is

A skin is a `Document` record with kind `note`. Its entire body is one JSON object,
with no Markdown fence or prose around it:

```json
{
  "schema": "native.app-skin.v1",
  "packages": ["agent.slack-workspace-v2"],
  "display_name": "Discord-like",
  "icon": "brand:discord",
  "tokens": {"--app-bg": "#313338", "--app-text": "#f2f3f5"},
  "css": ".win{border-radius:0}",
  "labels": {"channels": "Text channels"}
}
```

Only `schema` and `packages` are required; unknown fields reject the whole skin.

- `packages`: 1–16 exact package ids that may use this skin. No wildcards.
- `display_name`: shown instead of the app's record name. Non-blank, at most 128 characters.
- `icon`: shown instead of the app's `app_icon`. `brand:<slug>` (a Simple Icons slug such as
  `brand:discord`) or a PascalCase Lucide name such as `Gamepad2`. An unknown but well-formed
  name shows a monogram tile.
- `tokens`: replacement values for the app's `--app-*` custom properties.
- `css`: extra stylesheet, applied inside the app frame only.
- `labels`: replacement text for the app's published label keys.

Limits: 16 KiB for the whole body, 12 KiB for `css`, at most 128 tokens and 128 labels, at
most 512 characters per label or token value.

**Token values** are one of: a colour (hex such as `#5865f2`, a CSS colour name, `rgb()`,
`hsl()`, `oklch()` and similar, or `color-mix(in srgb, <colour> 30%, <colour>)`, which may
use `var(--app-…)`), a length (`16px`, `0.5rem`, `50%`, `0`), or a font-family list of names
(`system-ui, "Segoe UI", sans-serif`). Token names look like `--app-name`. Anything else
(`url(`, `;`, braces, `@`, backslashes, `expression`) rejects the skin.

**Cannot do:** load remote fonts or images (blocked by the app's sandbox), use
`@import` or `@charset` (rejected), add controls, change what a click does, rename real
records, channels or people, or touch Native's own chrome around the app. A skin changes
looks and wording only.

## Find what the app supports, from Native alone

1. **Find the installed app and its exact package id.** The installed app is a
   `Document` of kind `artifact`; its body is the app's HTML. The host reads the artifact
   that the install points at, so ask the install, not a search by name. HQ has many
   artifacts called "Slack" (old versions and candidates) and only one is installed. If you
   know the package id:

   ```json
   {"executor": "artifacts_read", "operation": "manage_alpha_tabs.inspect",
    "arguments": {"package": "agent.slack-workspace-v2"}}
   ```

   The result has `install.artifact_id` (the record to write to), `install.version` and
   `install.status`. HQ's Slack is `agent.slack-workspace-v2`. An app older than its
   skin-ready release (Slack before 0.5.0) has no tokens or label table, so `tokens` and
   `labels` will not visibly change it until it is updated; `display_name`, `icon` and
   `css` still apply. If you do not know the
   package id, call `manage_alpha_tabs.list` with `view:"summary"` to find a package
   (`package`, `name`, `version`, `status`, `artifact_id`, `event_id`); removed installs
   stay hidden unless `include_removed:true`. Then `inspect` one package for its full
   detail (event_id guard, adoption, launch binding).
   Both reads need hosted Native: they are not served from offline or member copies.

2. **See what presentation is already set** (cheap; it avoids reading the body):

   ```sql
   SELECT key, value FROM facet_values WHERE record_id = ?1 AND key IN ('app_skin', 'app_icon') ORDER BY key
   ```

   Pass the artifact id as `?1`. No `app_skin` row means the built-in look. To list existing
   skins, query by name (for example skins you named `Skin — …`), not by body; `query_sql`
   cannot read bodies over 256 KiB, and an artifact's body is far larger than that.

3. **Read what the app exposes.** `get_record` with `format: "json"` on the artifact id
   returns the HTML in `body`. Three things in it are the app's whole skin surface:

   - **Tokens:** the `--app-*` custom properties declared in the `:root { … }` block at the
     top of the stylesheet. Only these can be set in `tokens`.
   - **Label keys:** the JSON in
     `<script type="application/json" id="native-skin-labels">…</script>` in the head. Its
     keys are the only `labels` the app reads; its values are the defaults. Unknown keys do
     nothing. If this script is missing, the app is not skinnable for labels.
   - **Stable selectors:** elements carry `data-skin-region="…"` attributes. Prefer these in
     `css` over incidental class names.

   An app body is large (Slack's is about 650 KB), and there is no ranged read or SQL access
   to it. If your client cannot hold that, fetch it to a file or hand it to a helper that
   greps for `:root`, `native-skin-labels` and `data-skin-region`, or start from the Slack
   vocabulary below.

**Slack vocabulary (0.5.x).** Confirm against the installed body when you can.

- Twelve common tokens: `--app-bg` (main area), `--app-surface` (cards, composer),
  `--app-sidebar-bg`, `--app-rail-bg` (also the page behind the window), `--app-text`,
  `--app-muted`, `--app-faint`, `--app-line`, `--app-hover`, `--app-selected` (selected
  sidebar row), `--app-accent`, `--app-link`. About a hundred more cover fonts
  (`--app-font-sans`), radii (`--app-radius`, `--app-avatar-radius`), density, avatars and
  chrome (`--app-topbar-bg`, `--app-chrome-text`). The body editor takes
  `--app-editor-bg`, `--app-editor-text` and `--app-editor-link`.
- Labels: `workspaceName`, `workspaceInitial`, `workspace`, `searchPlaceholder`, `home`,
  `directMessages`, `activity`, `later`, `more`, `threads`, `draftsAndSent`, `channels`,
  `directMessagesHeading`, `agents`, `sessions`, `composerPrefix`, `replyPlaceholder`,
  `sourceName`.
- Regions: `topbar`, `search`, `rail`, `rail-item`, `workspace-tile`, `window`, `sidebar`,
  `sidebar-head`, `workspace-name`, `sidebar-section`, `sidebar-section-head`, `nav-row`
  (with `channel-row`, `dm-row`, `agent-row`, `session-row`), `main`, `channel-header`,
  `message-list`, `message`, `avatar`, `composer`, `thread-pane`.

## Recipes

Each write takes a `reason`. Name the records you relied on in `sources`.

**Create a skin.** `records_write.create_record`. The body is a JSON string; keep it pure
JSON. File it in a folder everyone who uses the app can read (default Unfiled is fine
inside one workspace):

```json
{"type": "Document", "kind": "note",
 "name": "Skin — Discord-like — Slack",
 "body": "{\"schema\":\"native.app-skin.v1\",\"packages\":[\"agent.slack-workspace-v2\"],\"display_name\":\"Discord-like\",\"icon\":\"brand:discord\",\"tokens\":{\"--app-accent\":\"#5865f2\"}}",
 "reason": "Discord-like look for the Slack app"}
```

**Activate it.** `records_write.update_record` on the *installed artifact*, not the skin:

```json
{"id": "<artifact_id>", "facets": {"app_skin": "<skin id>"},
 "reason": "Use the Discord-like skin", "sources": ["<skin id>"]}
```

**Edit the active skin live.** Rewrite the skin's body; the app repaints live and
no pointer write is needed. Body writes need a guard: read the skin with `get_record`
for its `body_digest`, then:

```json
{"id": "<skin id>", "body_set": "<complete new JSON>", "if_body_digest": "<digest>",
 "reason": "Darker sidebar"}
```

`body_replace` edits a span instead; the guard still applies.

**Switch** to another skin with the same activate call and a different id. **Clear** with
`{"id": "<artifact_id>", "facets": {"app_skin": null}, "reason": "Back to built-in"}`. The
skin notes remain in the library for next time.

**Loading takes a moment.** A skin the host has read before paints immediately. A switch to
one it has not read keeps the previous skin, quietly, until the new note loads, or until its
first read error, or 3 seconds, whichever comes first. After that the app falls back to the
built-in look with an "unreadable" notice, and a late successful read still applies the skin.
An app freshly opened with no skin to retain waits quietly for the read. So a palette that
has not changed yet, or a momentary notice, is not evidence that the JSON is wrong: re-read
the note and wait a few seconds before rewriting a valid skin.

**Rename or re-icon only.** Either write a skin with just `schema`, `packages` and
`display_name` and/or `icon` (reversible with one pointer write), or change the app record
itself: `update_record` with `name`, or `facets: {"app_icon": "brand:discord"}` (clear with
`null`). Each field resolves independently: the active skin's `display_name` or `icon`, if
it has one, wins over the artifact's `name` or `app_icon`, which win over the package
default. A skin with no `icon` keeps the artifact's.

**Scope.** `app_skin` sits on the artifact, so it is shared by everyone whose install uses
that artifact; there are no personal skins yet. Updating an app can move the install to a new
artifact record. After any app update, check the new artifact's name, `app_icon` and
`app_skin` (the `facet_values` query above) and re-apply whichever were reset. Newer
alpha-tab-kit versions carry these over, but do not rely on it.

## Worked example: Slack, Discord-like

A condensed version of the real fixture. It sets the twelve common tokens (backgrounds with
their text), the editor trio, round avatars and server tiles, and five labels:

```json
{
  "schema": "native.app-skin.v1",
  "packages": ["agent.slack-workspace", "agent.slack-workspace-v2"],
  "display_name": "Discord-like",
  "icon": "brand:discord",
  "tokens": {
    "--app-bg": "#313338", "--app-surface": "#2b2d31", "--app-sidebar-bg": "#2b2d31",
    "--app-rail-bg": "#1e1f22", "--app-text": "#f2f3f5", "--app-muted": "#b5bac1",
    "--app-faint": "#949ba4", "--app-line": "#3f4147", "--app-hover": "#2e3035",
    "--app-selected": "#404249", "--app-accent": "#5865f2", "--app-link": "#00a8fc",
    "--app-topbar-bg": "#1e1f22", "--app-editor-bg": "#313338",
    "--app-editor-text": "#f2f3f5", "--app-editor-link": "#00a8fc",
    "--app-tile-radius": "50%", "--app-avatar-radius": "50%", "--app-avatar-size": "40px"
  },
  "css": ":root{color-scheme:dark}.win{margin:0;border-radius:8px 0 0 0;box-shadow:none}.side{border-right:0}.side-head h1{font-size:15px}[data-skin-region=\"composer\"]{border-radius:8px}",
  "labels": {
    "workspaceName": "Native community", "workspace": "server", "channels": "Text channels",
    "directMessages": "Direct messages", "home": "Home"
  }
}
```

For maintainers, the full skin (118 tokens, 16 labels, the complete stylesheet) is
`packages/native-launcher/test/fixtures/discord-like.skin.json`, with a no-override
`slack-classic.skin.json` beside it.

## Pitfalls

- **Exact package ids.** The skin is ignored (with a notice) unless the app's package id is
  listed. HQ's Slack is `agent.slack-workspace-v2`; the plain `agent.slack-workspace` is
  another id. List every id you want to cover.
- **Pair backgrounds with text.** A dark `--app-bg` with the default dark `--app-text`
  is unreadable. Set `--app-bg` with `--app-text`, `--app-sidebar-bg` and
  `--app-rail-bg` with `--app-chrome-text`, and `--app-accent` with `--app-on-accent`.
  Always set `--app-editor-bg`, `--app-editor-text` and `--app-editor-link` together; the
  editor stays a light card otherwise.
- **Cascade order.** The host appends your token rules, then your `css`, at the end of
  `<head>`, after the app's own head styles. A style the app places in `<body>` or adds
  from script can still win at equal specificity. If a rule does not bite, raise its
  specificity (use the `data-skin-region` attribute) rather than adding `!important`
  everywhere.
- **Keep CSS modest.** Stylesheets can break layout (hidden controls, overflow, a search box
  that no longer fits). Prefer tokens, then small region rules, and have the person look at
  the result; you cannot see the pixels. Edit the skin body to iterate.
- **Do not edit the app's own HTML to restyle it.** That changes its digest and needs a new
  install and consent. A skin never does.
- **If a skin breaks the app, clear the pointer first.** Accepted CSS can still hide or
  break things (for example `body{display:none}`) and the host shows no notice for that.
  Set `app_skin` to `null` on the artifact to restore the built-in look at once, then fix
  the note and re-attach it.
- **Rejected or unreadable notes fall back safely.** The host uses the built-in look and
  shows "App skin unavailable (<reason>)", without hiding workspace data. Reasons: `size`, `json`, `schema`, `packages`,
  `incompatible` (the app's package id is not listed), `display_name`, `icon`, `tokens`,
  `labels`, `css`, `css_import`, `missing` (archived, or the wrong type or kind), `malformed`,
  `pointer` (`app_skin` is not a record UUID), `unreadable`.
- **Labels change wording, not data.** A label cannot rename a real channel, person or
  record.
